text: A guest book that knows who is coming. The lantern is lit.
picture: The Storyteller stands in a dark, misty hollow, holding a glowing red lantern low at his side. Mist curls around his boots. Far behind him, the faint, lonely outline of a motel in fog, one window lit. Mood: eerie, expectant.

text: I work the night desk at the Wayside Motel, out on Route 9, where the road runs between two towns that don't talk to each other.
picture: Exterior of a small, run-down, single-story motel at night surrounded by fog. A long row of identical doors. A single window is lit at the front office. An empty, two-lane road stretches away into darkness. Mood: isolated, uneasy.

text: Twelve rooms. Most nights, nobody comes.
picture: From inside the motel office, looking out the lit window at the long, empty, fog-shrouded row of dark motel room doors. No lights, no cars, no people. Mood: desolate, quiet.

text: The guest book sits open on the counter. The owner, Mr. Pell, likes ink.
picture: A worn wooden desk counter. An old leather guest book lies open. A fountain pen rests beside it. A single desk lamp casts a warm pool of light over it. A brass bell sits nearby. Mood: ordinary, slightly formal.
sound: the quiet hum of a lamp

text: He says a name in ink is a promise.
picture: Close-up on the open page of the guest book. The columns of faded, handwritten entries are barely legible. The fountain pen's nib gleams next to it, suggesting recent use. Mood: precise, ritualistic.

text: Every morning, when I hand over the keys, there's a new line in it. Room six.
picture: June at the counter in grey dawn light, looking tired. One hand holds a ring of motel keys. Her other hand's finger rests under a single, fresh line of dark blood-red ink in the open guest book. Mood: tired, uneasy, confused.

text: Signed at two fourteen a.m. A different name every night.
picture: Close-up on June's face, weary and pale in the dawn light, her gaze fixed on the single line written in blood-red ink, her expression a mix of exhaustion and quiet dread. Mood: uneasy, foreboding.

text: Room six has been boarded up since before I was hired.
picture: Exterior at night under a dim, yellow porch bulb. A single motel door is nailed shut with weathered grey planks. A brass number '6' hangs crookedly. Thick fog presses close against the doorframe. Mood: ominous, abandoned. 'red accent': none.
sound: a loose plank groaning in the wind

text: The first week, I blamed the day staff. The second week, I stopped blaming anyone. I started watching.
picture: June sits rigidly at the front desk, her phone held up in both hands for light and recoil. The open guest book glows red under the desk lamp. The black window behind her frames her isolation.

text: Last night, at two thirteen, the lights in the parking lot flickered.
picture: Close on the fountain pen lying askew on the open guest book's page. The dim desk lamp's light stutters, alternating between weak pool of yellow and darker, threatening shadow.

text: At two fourteen, the pen moved.
picture: A black-handled fountain pen sits on the guest book's page, its nib pointed in a different direction. No one's hand is near it. The desk lamp light gleams on its dark surface.
sound: the faint scrape of a nib

text: Not much. Just a roll. Like someone had brushed it with a sleeve.
picture: June's face, lit solely by the cold blue light of her phone screen. Her wide eyes are fixed on her phone, jaw tight and rigid. She refuses to look down at the book.

text: I didn't look at the book. I looked at the camera.
picture: June at the desk, face pale in screen-light, staring up at a security monitor mounted high on the wall. Her eyes are wide with horror. The dark office presses in around her.

text: On the screen, I was sitting at the desk.
picture: A hand holds a smartphone displaying the black-and-white CCTV feed. On the screen, June sits stiffly at the desk. The dark figure behind her is a menacing blur in the grainy footage.

text: And behind me, close enough to breathe on my neck, a
picture: June's face, frozen in midsentence, eyes wide, lips parted on the cut-off word 'a'. The cold desk lamp light sharpens her terror. Her breath is visible in the chilly air.

text: man in a wet raincoat was leaning over my shoulder to write.
picture: The same CCTV view, but now the hooded figure's right hand—pale, long-fingered—reaches into frame over June's shoulder. Its fingers hover just above the open guest book, poised to dip the red fountain pen.
sound: the scratch of a nib beginning an unseen stroke

text: I didn't turn around. I couldn't.
picture: From behind, June sits rigid at the desk, her head held perfectly still, refusing to turn. The darkness behind her is deep and close. Her shoulders are tense with fear.
sound: a single drop of water hitting the desk

text: When the lights came back, the office was empty.
picture: The motel office room is dimly lit by overhead fluorescent lights. The counter and chairs are empty, and the door to the back hall stands slightly open.

text: The book was open. The ink was still wet.
picture: A close view of the guest book open on the counter, a fresh line written in wet, dripping red ink, with a small puddle of water beside it.

text: Room six. Two fourteen a.m. And the name was mine.
picture: June Marsh's hands are braced on the counter beside the guest book, her face pale with terror as she stares down at the red ink entry bearing her name and room six.

text: Mr. Pell came in at six. He read the line very quietly.
picture: Mr. Pell stands behind the counter, leaning over the guest book, his face shadowed with deep sadness and resignation as he reads the red ink line.

text: Then he took a key off the hook.
picture: Mr. Pell's hand takes an old, tarnished brass key on a frayed red tag from a wooden pegboard hook behind the counter.
sound: the metallic jingle of the key

text: A key I had never seen. "It's always the one at the desk," he said. "Your room's ready."
picture: Mr. Pell holds the brass key out across the counter to June, his kind, sad eyes meeting hers. June, out of focus in the foreground, stands frozen.

text: The Wayside Motel is still open. The night desk is always staffed. And if you sign the book, check the name above yours.
picture: The Storyteller stands in the eerie hollow, his red lantern lowered by his side. Far behind him in the fog, the dark row of motel doors is visible, one boarded door standing open with a dim light inside.
